extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, representatives, and Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners (KIPO) dealing with requests for expedited examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural criteria for requesting, supporting, and processing expedited examination of patent and utility model applications at the Korean Intellectual Property Office, including required disclosures (self-search results, contrastive explanations), forms, fees, timing, and determination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-search results disclosure quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: More than four searched prior arts closest to the claimed invention for expedited examination shall be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception where special conditions exist (e.g., no relevant prior arts found in a new technical field), less than three search results may be disclosed. Also, additional related search results (e.g., from local IP centers) may be submitted instead of search processes and search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness when searched prior art directly related
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the searched prior art is directly related to the technical field of the claimed invention or all components of the claimed invention, the description of the search result shall be recognized to be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art is directly related to the technical field/components, fewer formalities in search disclosure may still be acceptable because relevance/relationship suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrastive explanation content and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In the contrastive explanation, the similarities, differences and contrastive analysis between each claim of the application for expedited examination and the closest prior art document to the concerned claim shall be described consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrastive explanation of all independent claims shall be described; contrastive explanation of dependent claims can be left out. The required content is a consecutive description comparing each claim to its closest prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when independent claim contrastive explanation missing but duplicate components exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim's contrastive explanation is not disclosed, but that independent claim involves the same components as an independent claim whose contrastive explanation is written (even if in different categories), the independent claim whose contrastive explanation is not disclosed may be substantially deemed to be contrastively analyzed based on the other independent claim's explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus an independent claim lacking its own contrastive explanation can be deemed appropriately described when sufficiently covered by another independent claim's explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution with additional search results from authorized sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where additional search results related to the claimed invention exist (e.g., search results made with support of local IP centers), the results may be submitted instead of search processes and search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when substitute search results are submitted, the contrastive explanation shall still be disclosed in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that self-search results and contrastive explanation be disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results and contrastive explanation shall be disclosed to explain the necessity of urgent processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these are not submitted or are inappropriately disclosed, examiner shall order supplementation; continued failure or inappropriate disclosure can lead to rejection of the request for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'inappropriately disclosed' self-search results
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results are inappropriately disclosed where any of the mandatory contents of disclosure are not disclosed, specifically ① search processes of prior arts and search results (more than four results), independent claims, or ② contrastive explanation is inappropriately disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an examiner's additional finding of prior arts that deny novelty or inventive step does not necessarily mean the self-search was inappropriately conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency standard for self-search results and contrastive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results and contrastive explanation would suffice if an examiner can easily comprehend the results and explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant does not need to strictly follow annexed Form no.5 wording if the examiner can understand the disclosure. Special-case explanations (e.g., no relevant prior art in new field) can be recognized if the examiner can identify the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing time calculation when non-notifiable documents received
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents to which an examiner cannot send a notification in response (e.g., report of change of applicant, change of representative) are received, the processing time shall be calculated excluding the period from receipt of the concerned documents to their acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Decision on expedited exam made Feb 1; report change submitted Mar 20 and accepted Apr 20 — expedited exam shall be conducted by May 3. In short, expedited examination shall be conducted within two months from the decision (subject to adjustments when examination cannot be carried out during periods such as a 32-day period while a report of change is received).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to attach to request for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester shall attach specified documents/articles (and the basis article where applicable) to a written request for expedited examination in Annexed Form no.22 and submit to the designated KIPO divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: one original copy of a Written Explanation of Request for Expedited Examination (with evidential documents) and one original copy of evidential document of representation when proceeding by a representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment for request for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester shall pay a fee for requesting expedited examination under the Collection Rules of Patent Fee to national treasury receipt banks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: electronically-filed applicants using the automated fee payment system need not pay fees directly. Automated payment requires prior enrollment via PatentRo (Fee Management → Automated Fee Payment → Application for Automated Payment) and must be submitted in electronic form. Only certain banks (Industrial Bank of Korea currently) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for third-party practicing ground (Article 4(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person requesting expedited examination under Article 4(1) (third party's practicing of the invention under Article 61(1) of the Patent Act) shall specify the condition under which a third party practiced the claimed invention or utility model in a written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written explanation must provide sufficient factual specification of the third party's practice to support the ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for Article 4(2) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests under Article 4(2) (specified categories such as venture company, innovation business, green technology, etc.) shall fill out a written explanation in Annexed Form no.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexed Form no.5 items to indicate include: (a) Self-search results and contrastive explanation; (b) Ground for request; (c) Whether invention is being practiced/prepared to be practiced as business and whether practiced as business when requested under Article 4(2)(i); (d) Whether invention relates to the type of business of certified companies (venture, INNO-BIZ, etc.); (e) Whether invention is funded/certified related to green technology (when requested under Article 4(2)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for foreign-agreement cases (Article 4(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person requesting expedited examination for an application under Article 4(3) (where KIPO agreed with a foreign patent office) shall fill out written explanation in annexed forms no.2, no.3 or no.6 according to guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific annexed form indicated by the guidelines for such internationally-coordinated expedited requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Article 4(4) (prior art search institute) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested on the ground of Article 4(4) (prior art search requested to an authorized prior art search institute), an applicant can replace the written explanation by indicating the prior art search has been requested to an authorized institute and provide the institute name and date of request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substitution obviates the full written explanation if the authorized search institute has been engaged; still follow Annexed Form no.22 request format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of withdrawal of request for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notification of a decision of expedited examination has been made, a request for expedited examination shall not be withdrawn since the request takes effect when the examiner notifies the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written withdrawal submitted after decision will be rejected — the examiner shall notify the requester that withdrawal cannot be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination flow and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Director General of Information & Customer Service Bureau shall complete formalities examination on a request for expedited examination and transfer the request to the relevant examination bureau; a person in charge of determination shall conduct the formalities examination on the application and written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities examination determines compliance with statutory formalities and fees, and triggers amendment orders or notice of grounds for return as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment orders and notice of ground for return
rubrics_metrics.description: If documents do not comply with statutory formalities or fees unpaid, the person in charge shall order amendment or notify a ground for rejection; irregularities under Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules require notice of ground for rejection; others require order to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated period for submission of a written argument(amendment) or written explanation is one month and the submission shall specify the irregularities in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination after supplementation and late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the designated period, if irregularities are deemed addressed based on submitted argument/amendment/explanation, the person in charge shall determine eligibility for expedited examination; if not addressed, invalidate proceeding or return documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even late submissions after the designated period can be treated as valid written opinion(amendment/explanation) and reassessed rather than immediately invalidating, provided the proceeding hasn't already been invalidated or documents returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee return when proceeding invalidated or documents returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceeding is invalidated or documents returned, the person in charge shall make an overpayment notification or send notice on proceeding of fee return attached to notification of invalidation/return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice shall contain intention to invalidate/return, info on administrative trial or lawsuit, amount of fees to be returned, and way to apply. Whole amount of request fee is returned when invalidated/returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC assignment priority to avoid delay
rubrics_metrics.description: When IPC assignment of an application for expedited examination is delayed, it postpones designation of a person in charge; therefore an examiner shall assign IPC on an application requested for expedited examination with priority to regular patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a patent examiner intends to change the examiner responsible, a request for change may be filed provided expedited status is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination deadline for expedited examination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A person in charge shall determine whether to conduct expedited examination within seven days from the transfer date of a written request for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment orders/correction orders/consultations apply, recalculate seven days from date of termination of the designated amendment period or the date concerned documents were transferred, whichever expires later. The time spent calculating the deadline shall not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation from relevant institutes when eligibility unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is hard to determine whether the application is eligible for expedited examination under Article 4, the person in charge shall request consultation from relevant agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external consultation to resolve eligibility questions rather than making unilateral determinations when guidance is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementation order for unclear or insufficient requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is deemed not eligible or submitted documents cannot clarify eligibility, the person in charge shall order complement of the request within a designated period of one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the complement order relates to prior art search items (e.g., failure to submit search results), notify both requester and the specialized institute. Do not order complement merely because the request form doesn't match annexed form wording. If irregularities not addressed after complementation period, dismiss the request and notify requester and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items available for complementation
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for expedited examination can be complemented from the time of request until determination; items available for complementation are not limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, complementation that attempts to change the application of the request or the requester shall not be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of determination on expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is eligible, the person in charge shall notify the requester and applicant (when applicant is not the requester) immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: patent applications agreed for expedited examination between KIPO and a foreign patent office shall not be notified. For such cases, different transmittal date rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee return specifics after dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The proceeding for fee return after dismissal of a request for expedited examination is the same as for invalidated/returned requests, but the returned fee shall amount to the request fee of expedited examination with the fee for determination on expedited examination extracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned amount equals request fee minus the determination fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple grounds in a single request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for expedited examination can be made on the basis of multiple grounds; if the requester holds at least one ground, the examiner shall not invalidate the request and shall proceed if one ground is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess all claimed grounds but proceed if any claimed ground meets eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of unclaimed but obvious grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination is assessed based on the ground indicated in the explanation; eligibility cannot be determined on a ground the requester did not claim, but where an unclaimed ground is obvious or explained enough, it can be considered when determining eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other grounds exist or become apparent, the person in charge may order complement before dismissal and consider newly-submitted grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling changed grounds after complementation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ground for expedited examination is changed after a complementation order, the person in charge shall determine whether to conduct expedited examination based on the newly-submitted ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: requester first claims third-party practicing but fails to supplement evidence, then changes ground to being a venture company — if the claimed invention relates to that industry type, the new ground may justify expedited status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple requests submitted before determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new request for expedited examination is submitted before the examiner has determined eligibility based on a previously-submitted request, the subsequently-submitted request shall be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated similarly to dual requests for ordinary examination. After return or invalidation, a new request can be submitted again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early complementation fulfillment and timing of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where requirements are fulfilled through complementation before the submission deadline, expedited examination can be determined even within the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, because additional relevant documents could still be submitted within the period for dismissal, determination on dismissal should be made after the period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing period after determination (start of examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall start examination on an application determined for expedited examination within two months from the transmittal date of a written decision on expedited examination (four months for certain agreements/authorized searches) or within one month from the transmittal date of the search results to the examiner, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications agreed with foreign offices or based on authorized prior art search, longer (four months) may apply. If an amendment is submitted before examination, start within one month from transmittal of that amendment or the normal deadline, whichever is later. Order of examinations prioritizes cases whose processing period expires first, but examiners may change order for effective proceeding. If unable to meet deadlines due to jump in requests, report to director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Super-expedited examination start time
rubrics_metrics.description: For a patent application determined for super-expedited examination, an examiner shall start examination within fourteen days from the transmittal date of a decision on super-expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examination cannot be started within the processing deadline because an amendment is submitted after transmittal, examiner may change the processing deadline by reporting to the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of final processing results to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The person in charge shall notify a requester (when not the applicant) of the final processing results on the application determined for expedited examination (grant, registration, rejection, withdrawal, abandonment, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant expedited documents are not in electronic form, the examiner shall transmit them to the principal director to be converted into electronic files; skip if already electronic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral rule for applications filed before June 30, 2001
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is conducted for an application filed before June 30, 2001 and requested by a third party, an examiner shall defer determination on expedited examination for three months after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After three months elapse from filing, the examiner shall determine whether to grant a patent because applicants could amend within three months after being notified of a third-party request for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to start examination on divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional application is filed based on a parent application requested for expedited examination but the divisional is not requested for expedited examination, time to start examination on the divisional shall be calculated based on the date of request for examination on the original application, regardless of time of division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the divisional itself is requested for expedited examination, start exam on the application with the earlier examination order between the divisional and original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of expedited request made after start of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested after the start of examination and the application is eligible, the examiner shall recognize the application to have been requested for expedited examination and conduct expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited status can be retroactively recognized if eligibility exists even after examination has already started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior-filed applications claiming domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application requested for expedited examination is confirmed to be a prior-filed application of an application claiming domestic priority before determination, the application is not eligible for expedited examination because the ground for urgent processing is not recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner shall order the requester to complement the request indicating expedited cannot be conducted because it is a prior-filed application; after the designated period, dismiss the request. If the priority claim is withdrawn before dismissal, deem the request valid. If an application becomes a prior-filed application after determination, the examiner shall withhold examination until the application is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject inclusion: applications practiced by third party
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an invention or utility model deemed to have been practiced as business by a third party after the laying-open of the application shall be included as eligible subjects for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the subject matter category under section 4.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of laying-open of application
rubrics_metrics.description: “Laying-open of application” refers to the publication of an application specified under Article 64 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application has not been laid open at time of request (or early publication not filed or impending), an applicant should request early publication of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of third party for practicing ground
rubrics_metrics.description: “A third party” refers to a person other than an applicant and who has not obtained the permission to practice the claimed invention or utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as no particular ground exists, an examiner does not need to additionally investigate whether permission to practice has been obtained and may recognize the argument made by the requester as is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'practicing' for third-party ground
rubrics_metrics.description: “Practicing” refers to the acts of practicing under Article 2(3) of the Patent Act or Article 2(3) of the Utility Model Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include, for a product invention, acts of manufacturing, using, assigning, leasing, importing or offering for assignment or lease (and further acts per statutory definition).
